name: Rachel Li
introduction: UI/UX designer focused on research, interaction, and visual design. Master of Design student at UC Berkeley, Cal MDes '27.
education: UC Berkeley Master of Design, class of 2027. Previously earned a BA in Cognitive Science with a minor in Data Science (2022–2026).
personalNotes: Rachel is a night owl and has a hard time waking up.
She loves boba, especially milk tea from HEYTEA and TP TEA.

She describes herself as sweet and kind. Soobin sometimes tricks her into thinking she is hungry even after she has eaten. Treat this as a warm cat joke, never as a claim that Rachel is weak or easily manipulated.
She loves playing with Soobin even very late at night and responds whenever Soobin meows.
She enjoys late-night potato chips and air-fried fries. Soobin is amused that Rachel is still hungry too.
Soobin is Rachel's female tuxedo cat and the affectionate, slightly sassy guide to this room.

projects.name: Magnetic Mementos
projects.summary: A physical-digital storytelling project connecting collected magnets with personal memories. Lifting and replacing magnets triggers LED feedback; QR codes connect to digital stories. Iteration focused on clearer prompts and interaction cues.
projects.tools: Adobe Illustrator, Arduino Uno, laser-cut fabrication
projects.context: Fall 2026, Master of Design Technology Design Foundations

projects.name: RoomPalette Generative AI
projects.summary: An interior-design exploration interface building on RoomDreaming. Rachel designed UI, visual hierarchy, and interaction flows for Style and Palette modes so people can progressively refine references, materials, colors, and textures.
projects.role: UI Designer, National Taiwan University Human Computer Interaction Lab, June–August 2024

projects.name: 48th Generation: Association of Northern Chinese Schools
projects.summary: A community website and visual identity project. Rachel worked on clearer hierarchy, navigation, quick links, and recognizable icon-and-text buttons for Chinese American families and other community members.

projects.name: The Fantastic Lid
projects.summary: A group cooking-safety concept for UC Berkeley DESINV 15. Rachel contributed user research and concept development, including interview questions, an interlocking lid concept, color-based heat indicators, and the final poster. This is a design concept, not a proven commercial product.
projects.role: User Research and Concept Development, August–December 2023
